label: declaration-placement-and-file-organization
name: A declaration, constant block, include or growing function sits where a reader will not look for it
description: What breaks: findability. constexpr constants buried mid-file in hwattention.hpp (2947931435 'can we move all these constexpr to the top', then conceded to config.hpp); pos_driver_register_fuse_stats declared in alloc.hpp though unrelated to memory alloc (3405003751 'an odd place to declare this'); float error helpers in bf16.hpp (2760690084 'good enough for now though'); "spdlog/spdlog.h" with quotes and apart from the file's <spdlog/fmt/fmt.h> (3405979630); hw_prepare already several hundred lines and both branches growing (3405172585 'pull these stanzas into helper utilities ... Next iteration would be fine'); debug dump functions cluttering the main hardware-attention header (2948027543, offers an hwattention_debug module). Procedure: for added namespace-scope constants check they precede the first function/struct or live in the config header; for each added declaration compare the header's topic with the declaration's subsystem; for each added third-party include match the file's bracket style and grouping; for a function the diff grows past a few hundred lines along parallel branches suggest named helpers; for debug helpers in a production header suggest a sibling module. All nits; several explicitly deferred to a later iteration.
disposition_reason: No existing check looks at placement; 6 rows over 3 PRs, mechanical for position and include style.
agent_feasibility: yes: file-position and include-style checks are mechanical; header-topic mismatch needs reading the header comment.

members.concern: The constexpr constants of the hardware-attention header (hwkv_pages_per_layer, hwkv_tok_per_page, hwkv_pchannel_page_size_B and siblings) sit in the middle of the file; Wade asks to move them to the top so a reader can find them.

detection.trigger: A header hunk adds, keeps or moves a block of `constexpr` / `inline constexpr` definitions that sits after function or struct definitions (not in the first N lines of the file and not in a config header).
detection.procedure: For each touched header, list line numbers of `constexpr` definitions at namespace scope (grep -n 'constexpr' FILE at HEAD) and the line of the first function or struct body; flag constants defined after it. Check whether a config header for the same subsystem exists (h/pos/config.hpp) and whether another reviewer already asked for the move.
detection.question: Is a namespace-scope constant defined below the first function or struct of the file, so that a reader must search the file body to locate it?

members.quote: kinda pedantic, but can we move all these constexpr to the top of this file :). It drives me nuts trying to (re)locate these sometimes, buried in the middle of the code like this
members.note: Wade self-replied (2949458908) deferring to mcherba's request to move them into config.hpp. Author: 'fixed in commit 8a6db7243'. Verified: 8a6db72438 adds 6 lines to h/pos/config.hpp; at head 429249ead6 hwkv_tok_per_page and hwkv_pchannel_page_size_B are at h/pos/config.hpp:90-91 and hwattention.hpp:450 keeps only a comment naming them.

members.concern: The new function declaration pos_driver_register_fuse_stats (registers per-device weight-reuse counters with FUSE, the file-system stats interface) sits in alloc.hpp, the HBM memory allocator header, where it has nothing to do with the file's topic; Wade asks to move it, suggesting lib.hpp.

detection.trigger: a diff adds a declaration (free function, struct, macro) to a header whose file name and header comment describe a different subsystem than the declaration's own comment or implementation
detection.procedure: for each added declaration in h/, read the header's top comment and the existing declarations around the hunk; read the definition in src/ and list what it touches (here: PosDevice fields and fuse stats, not the allocator); grep h/ for the header that declares the sibling symbols the definition uses (PosDevice lives in h/pos/device.hpp)
detection.question: Does the header that receives the declaration own the subsystem the declaration belongs to, or is there a header that already declares the symbols the new function operates on?

members.quote: just a nit, but this seems like an odd place to declare this new function? It doesn't really have anything to do with memory alloc. Although I don't really have a better suggestion either ;-p. Maybe `lib.hpp`?
members.note: At edec446b76 the declaration sat right below pos_devices_register_fuse_stats (allocator stats) in h/pos/alloc.hpp:231-234. Author replied it was supposed to be moved already; final head a62d15a3dc has it at h/pos/device.hpp:665 and alloc.hpp no longer declares it (verified with git show). Commit subject 'move fuse function declaration to corret place' is the fix.

members.concern: Wade says the new relative/absolute/combined error helpers operate on floats, so the bf16 header is an odd place for them, but accepts the placement for now.

detection.trigger: A PR adds free functions to a type's header (here bf16.hpp) whose parameter types do not name that type.
detection.procedure: Read the added function signatures; list their parameter types. If none is the header's own type, grep h/common for a header whose subject matches the parameter types (a float or numerics utilities header). Report placement as a nit with the better home named, or accept with 'for now' if the PR body states the reason (here: 'available wherever we're potentially comparing bf16 values').
detection.question: Do the added functions take or return the type this header defines, or do they belong in a more general numerics header?

members.quote: seems like an odd spot for these, lol... especially since they are generically operating on floats... good enough for now though!
members.note: The digest's diff hunk shows only context lines after `operator"" _bf16` (bf16.hpp:101-103); the 33 added lines are the inline error helpers per the PR body. No author reply; Wade approved in the same minute. Severity 'minor' is my reading of 'good enough for now'; he did not write nit.

members.concern: A third-party header is included with quotes ("spdlog/spdlog.h") instead of angle brackets, and it is separated from the existing <spdlog/fmt/fmt.h> include; Wade supplies the angle-bracket form and asks to group them.

detection.trigger: a diff adds an #include with double quotes whose path names a third-party or system library (spdlog, fmt, catch2, nlohmann, pci) rather than a project header under h/
detection.procedure: for each added #include "..." line, check whether the path resolves under the project's h/ tree; if not, it is third-party and the file's existing includes show the convention (device.cpp already had #include <spdlog/fmt/fmt.h>); also check whether the new include lands next to its sibling group
detection.question: Does the added include match the file's existing convention for third-party headers (angle brackets, grouped with the same library's other includes)?

members.quote:

... and group it with ` #include <spdlog/fmt/fmt.h>` down below maybe?
members.note: Verified at 247c8a4c22 device.cpp:12 had #include "spdlog/spdlog.h" and :18 had #include <spdlog/fmt/fmt.h>. At a62d15a3dc the include is <spdlog/spdlog.h>  // IWYU pragma: keep, placed directly after <spdlog/fmt/fmt.h>. This contradicts the skill's current sentence that Wade 'does not comment on formatting': he does comment on include style and grouping when it is a one-line suggestion.

members.concern: hw_prepare is already very long and the PR grows both its legacy-matmul and hardware-attention branches; Wade asks to extract the two stanzas into helper functions, acceptable as a next-iteration task.

detection.trigger: a diff adds many lines (tens or more) inside the body of a function that is already several hundred lines long, especially inside parallel branches of one if/else
detection.procedure: for each function the diff touches, measure its length at BASE and at HEAD (awk over the brace-balanced body, or clang's function ranges); if it grows and is already beyond roughly 200 lines, list the branch bodies that could be named helpers (here: the !workreq->attn_req legacy stanza starting at worker.cpp:1232 and the else attention stanza starting at :1326 at 247c8a4c22)
detection.question: Does the change enlarge an already oversized function along a branch that could be a named helper, and is the author willing to schedule the split?

members.quote: I really think we should pull these "legacy" and "hw-attn" stanzas into helper utilities.. this function is already so long, and now we're growing each branch even more. I was gonna do that awhile back and dropped off the radar. Next iteration would be fine though...
members.note: Author agreed to do it in the next phase; no code change in this PR. Wade explicitly deferred ('Next iteration would be fine'), so this did not block approval. At 247c8a4c22 the if (!workreq->attn_req) branch spans lines 1232-1326 and the else branch continues past 1460.

members.concern: Agreeing with mcherba that the debug dump functions should be kept, Wade proposes they live in their own 'hwattention_debug' module so the main hardware-attention header is less cluttered, and offers to do it himself later.

detection.trigger: A header that holds the production API also holds (or the diff adds/removes) a block of debug, dump or trace helpers (names containing dump_, debug_, print_, trace_) of substantial size.
detection.procedure: Count lines of debug/dump helpers in the touched header (grep -n 'dump_\|debug' FILE) versus the file total; check whether a sibling *_dump.hpp or *_debug.hpp already exists; check whether the PR removes the helpers outright (another reviewer may want them kept).
detection.question: Would moving the debug helpers to a sibling module leave the main header holding only the production API, without losing a debug capability another reviewer relies on?

members.quote: If it's not too much of a diversion, IMO ideally all these debug functions could live an a 'hwattention_debug' module, just to unclutter this main module a bit and better organize things? That's something I could take on in a later iteration though.
members.note: Reply to mcherba's request to keep dump commands as shard-aware versions. Outcome: commit 'Add shard-aware debug dump functions in pos/hwattention_dump.hpp' (h/pos/hwattention_dump.hpp +767 at head). form is a proposal in prose, not a ```suggestion block; recorded as suggestion_block for lack of a closer enum (it is an offered design change, not an ask or a question). Severity softened by 'Don't want to bog Brian down, lol'.
